draft.title: Sustainability of the current account
card: A current account deficit is easier to sustain if the borrowing behind it is used well. Foreign funds that pay for productive investment, such as mines, ports and machinery, can raise future output.
Export growth helps too. Stronger export income gives a country more foreign currency to pay what it owes overseas.
Borrowing used mainly for consumption adds to what is owed but does little to raise future income. This makes a deficit more of a worry.
the share of export income used to pay interest on foreign debt. A higher ratio means less export income is left for other uses, and a lower ratio means the debt is easier to carry.
draft.remember: A deficit is easier to carry when borrowing builds future income and the debt servicing ratio is low.

a.q: Which change would make Australia's debt servicing ratio fall?
opts: Export income rises while interest payments stay the same
Interest payments rise while export income stays the same
Export income falls while interest payments stay the same
Interest and export income both fall by the same share
a.why: The ratio is interest payments as a share of export income. If export income rises and interest stays the same, the share falls. If both fall by the same share, the ratio stays the same, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think of interest payments as a share of export income.

b.q: Two countries have the same current account deficit. Country X borrows to build export mines. Country Y borrows to fund extra spending on imported goods. Which statement is best?
opts: X's deficit is easier to carry, as its mines can lift exports
Y's deficit is easier to carry, as imports lift living standards
Both are equally easy to carry, as the deficits are the same
Neither can be carried, as any deficit leads to a crisis
b.why: Borrowing for export mines can raise future export income, which helps pay what is owed. Borrowing for spending adds to debt but does not raise future income, so Y's deficit is harder to carry. The deficits are the same size, but the use of funds differs, so the third option is tempting but wrong.
b.clue: Same size does not mean same use of the borrowed funds.
